support_examples.title: How to Remove Reccuring Events Sitemap Created by Events Calendar?
support_examples.description: Replies: 3 Hello, I work for a digital marketing company. On one of the websites we manage, we use the Events Calendar plugin to showcase upcoming events. Series of recurring events are part of this, and a sitemap (tec_recurring_events-sitemap.xml) was created through the plugin to store them within the sitemap index. However, many of these event pages are going to be outdated and we don’t want all of them to be crawling and indexed, so I have been trying to remove the sitemap from the index (we don’t want to remove the pages outright, only keep them from indexing). While the sitemap appears in the index created by the Yoast SEO plugin, there is no option to specifically remove this sitemap through Yoast SEO’s setting. Is there a way we set it up so the recurring events sitemap is removed from the index, without removing the actual recurring events from the site’s archives? support_examples.title: [NSFW] Yoast SEO metabox crashes with “e.isBeta is not a
support_examples.description: Replies: 3 Bug Report: Yoast SEO metabox crashes with “e.isBeta is not a function” in Post/Service editorEnvironment WordPress version: 7.1 Yoast SEO version: 28.3 (Free) PHP version: 8.4 Site URL: nano-tox.com Affected screens: Post editor, Service (custom post type) editor — occurs on both new and existing content Active caching: LiteSpeed Cache Relevant plugins active: WPCode, Slider Revolution, WP File Manager, MC4WP, CookieYes Summary The Yoast SEO metabox in the block editor intermittently crashes with a JavaScript error and displays: “Something went wrong. An unexpected error occurred.” e.isBeta is not a function. (In 'e.isBeta()', 'e.isBeta' is undefined) The crash is intermittent: on some page loads the metabox renders correctly (SEO analysis, Readability analysis, Schema tab, etc. all display and function normally), but on others — including after a hard refresh — the panel crashes a few seconds after initially rendering correctly.Steps to reproduce Open any post/page/custom post type in the block editor. Wait for the page to fully load. The Yoast SEO metabox initially renders normally (see Screenshot 1). After a few seconds, the metabox crashes and displays the “Something went wrong” error (see Screenshot 2). This does not happen on every load — it’s intermittent, but happens frequently, including on repeated hard refreshes. Console output Full error with stack trace: TypeError: e.isBeta is not a function. (In 'e.isBeta()', 'e.isBeta' is undefined) at zs — externals-components.js:80:4019 at Gs — externals-components.js:80:5112 at componentDidUpdate — externals-components.js:84:1448 at Ji — react-dom.min.js:180:99 at Hi — react-dom.min.js:179:281 at Hk — react-dom.min.js:178:332 at Rk — react-dom.min.js:197:315 at xb — react-dom.min.js:196:169 at Li — react-dom.min.js:189:376 at db — react-dom.min.js:79:184 at (anonymous) — react-dom.min.js:184:292 The selected/crashing DOM element at the time of the error is: ... This suggests the crash occurs specifically while Yoast is trying to render an error state. Additional relevant console warning appearing on the same page loads: wp.compose.pure is deprecated since version 7.1. Please use memo or PureComponent instead instead. This points to a likely compatibility issue between Yoast SEO’s editor integration and WordPress 7.1’s Block Editor / @wordpress/compose package changes.Network findings Multiple admin-ajax.php requests fire on the editor screen (Heartbeat API, etc.) — most return successfully (200, normal Heartbeat payloads like wp-refresh-post-lock , wp-auth-check ). At least one admin-ajax.php request was observed failing with: XMLHttpRequest cannot load https://nano-tox.com/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php due to access control checks. This occurred via load-scripts.php → heartbeat.min.js , not clearly isolated to a specific Yoast action yet. What we’ve already tried (did NOT resolve the issue) Disabled Yoast AI feature Disabled Schema Aggregation endpoint feature Disabled llms.txt feature Purged LiteSpeed Cache (server + browser) and hard-refreshed Deactivated/reactivated Yoast SEO Confirmed Yoast SEO is on the latest available version (28.3) Tested with a WPCode snippet (“Completely Disable Comments”) deactivated — no change Checked browser console across multiple reloads — error is reproducible but timing/trigger is not 100% consistent Suspected cause Given the wp.compose.pure deprecation warning appearing consistently alongside the crash, and the fact that the crash happens a few seconds after a successful initial render (suggesting an async state update failing on a component that expected a stable prop/context shape), we suspect this is a compatibility issue between Yoast SEO 28.3’s editor integration and WordPress 7.1’s Block Editor , rather than a conflict with a specific third-party plugin.Attachments Screenshot 1: Yoast SEO metabox rendering normally on initial load Screenshot 2: Yoast SEO metabox crash screen with the e.isBeta error Screenshot 3: Full console error with stack trace Screenshot 4: Console output showing the wp.compose.pure deprecation warning alongside the crash Request Could you confirm whether this is a known compatibility issue with WordPress 7.1, and if there’s a fix planned or a workaround we can apply in the meantime? Thank you!

support_examples.title: Custom accept link in Contact Form 7 mail is not being replaced
support_examples.description: Replies: 0 I am building a WordPress site using Contact Form 7 and WPCode. The purpose is to let an organiser submit a concert request. The request is stored as a pending request, and the email sent to me should contain a clickable “ACCEPTER FORESPØRGSEL” button. Clicking the button should change the request status and mark the selected date as occupied. The form ID is: 238e45a In the CF7 form I currently have: [hidden nk-accept-link] And in the mail template I have: [nk-accept-link] I have tried implementing this as a custom special mail tag using: add_filter( 'wpcf7_special_mail_tags', 'nk_acceptlink_special_mail_tag', 30, 3 ); I have also tried replacing the tag through: add_filter( 'wpcf7_mail_components', 'nk_acceptlink_direkte_i_mail', 999, 3 ); The PHP code successfully activates in WPCode, and the CF7 email is sent correctly. However, the received email still contains: [nk-accept-link] instead of the generated HTML link/button. Interestingly, the email is sometimes received before the other notification email, so I am wondering whether this could be related to the order in which Contact Form 7 processes mail tags and mail components. What is the correct/recommended way to create a dynamic accept link in a Contact Form 7 mail, where the URL depends on data created during the current form submission? Is wpcf7_special_mail_tags the correct hook for this, or should this be handled differently? I would particularly like to avoid adding more snippets until I understand which part of the CF7 mail-processing sequence I should be using. The desired result is simply: ACCEPTER FORESPØRGSEL [button/link] where the URL contains the unique token for the pending request. Any advice on the correct CF7 hook or approach would be greatly appreciated.

support_examples.title: Unexpected wpautop results
support_examples.description: Replies: 0 I have a website with wpautop disabled for WPCF7 forms and enabled for their emails, because some forms on the website have emails which need wpautop for their correct presentation. Some other forms have an email that doesn’t need wpautop. I think that this should not be a problem if these are full-html body-content emails (with in the editor the option “Use html content type” enabled), right? However, that is not the case. For example, suppose the email content contains a table with a cell [your_name] . When I process the email content with the WordPress function wpautop, outside the WPCF7 plugin,, I get the same text, albeit split over three lines: opening tag, cell content, closing tag: [your_name] That is perfectly all right. The email produced by WPCF7, however, contains (when I put everything back on one line): [your_name] . As a consequence, the cell content is presented in the email received with paragraph styling, resulting in 32px margin between the table rows. Is there a way to prevent this, other than adding a element to the email content to (in this case) reset the styling? Or is there a way to set the email wpautop on/off specific for each form? I checked $_POST in a wpcf7_autop_or_not filter function, but I didn’t find the information for which form it was going to send an email. Thank you in advance for your help!

support_examples.title: “Additional tax classes” field missing (WC11.0.1)
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 hi everyone, I’m running WooCommerce 11.0.1 and the “Additional tax classes” field is completely missing from WooCommerce → Settings → Tax → Tax Options . This is the field that normally lets you add classes like “Reduced rate” / “Zero rate” and is documented here: https://woocommerce.com/document/setting-up-taxes-in-woocommerce/configuring-specific-tax-setups-in-woocommerce/ What I need: Two tax classes — Standard (7%, currently used for coffee products) and a second class for 19% (for new tableware/dishware products). What I already checked and ruled out: “Enable tax rates and calculations” is active, the Tax tab itself works and Standard rates can be edited normally. “Automated taxes” is disabled (confirmed via WooCommerce → Status). The “Stripe Tax” extension is installed but “Enable Stripe Tax” is unchecked. The “WooCommerce Tax” extension was deactivated — no change. Tested in a private/incognito browser window — no change (rules out caching/browser extensions). Viewed page source (Ctrl+U) on the Tax Options page and searched for “tax_classes” and “Additional” — neither string appears anywhere in the HTML , so the field isn’t just hidden by CSS/JS, it’s not being rendered server-side at all. The product edit screen (Data → General → Tax class) also only shows “Standard” in the dropdown — no “Reduced rate”/”Zero rate” options either, and no way to add a new class from there. Active plugins that might be relevant: WooCommerce Germanized, Stripe Tax (v2.0.5). Theme: Betheme. My question: Has anyone seen a plugin (Germanized or otherwise) that removes the woocommerce_tax_classes setting field entirely via the woocommerce_tax_settings filter (or similar)? Or is this a known WooCommerce 11.0.1 bug? I’d like to understand whether this is a plugin conflict I can resolve myself, or something that needs a bug report. Thanks in advance for any pointers!

support_examples.title: Issue with Coupon Discount Rounding (The order is created manually)
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 I am encountering an issue with coupon discount rounding in WooCommerce orders. In the total price, as shown in the example, the difference is 2 cents. The problem only occurs when an order is created manually through the admin panel. If the order is placed normally—by adding items to the cart and entering a discount code—the total is calculated correctly. We use a completely clean system with no plugins and standard settings, except for the tax settings. support_examples.title: Wordfence warning about WPForms vulnerability
support_examples.description: Replies: 3 “The WPForms Pro plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Single Line Text and Paragraph Text Field Values in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.0.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit relies on the plugin’s own wp_kses_allowed_html filter widening the ‘post’ allowlist to permit iframe elements with a data-src attribute, which is not on WordPress’s URI-attribute sanitization list, allowing a javascript: URI stored in data-src to survive kses processing and subsequently be promoted to a live src attribute by the bundled admin script view-entry.min.js.”

support_examples.title: Notification settings and reality mismatch
support_examples.description: Replies: 3 v2.0.0.2 Forms are set to Ajax. Only cache is W3TC page cache. Embedded via Elementor widget. The notification settings appeared to be set to send email to admin with form contents and NO receipt to users, but some of the forms were doing something completely different – sending a receipt notification to form submitters and NOT to admin at all. I can’t remember if it was supposed to be doing both – I suspect yes because the receipts were well written specifically for the users of the site. This means for time unknown, emails were not being sent to admin for some forms. I suspect not that long because they are only just getting people questioning them. Maybe around 5th August (first person to alert us submitted then). Making a small change and pressing save fixed it (so what was appearing in settings then matched what happened in real life). So it seems that there used to be two notifications for each form (one for admin and one for user receipt) but one was being hidden and still in use and the one displayed in settings was being ignored. Have there been any other reports similar to this? Cheers keep up the good work

support_examples.title: Cloudflare Turnstile Siteverify Not Called in WPForms AJAX
support_examples.description: Replies: 4 Hello, I’ve encountered an unusual issue while using WPForms with Cloudflare Turnstile and would like to confirm this with technical support: Test Results: With AJAX submission disabled (standard full-page refresh): Everything works normally after the form is submitted—emails are sent, and the Cloudflare dashboard correctly logs the Siteverify verification requests to the backend. With AJAX submission enabled (refresh-free submission): Although the form submits normally and emails are sent successfully, the official Cloudflare dashboard continuously reports an error stating that Siteverify was not called. My Troubleshooting and Logical Verification: In the browser console during AJAX submission, I consistently capture this specific error: [Cloudflare Turnstile] Cannot find widget cf-chl-widgett-Vyllf, consider using turnstile.remove() to clean up a widget. I have confirmed that regardless of whether AJAX is enabled, the frontend correctly generates and includes the cf-turnstile-response token during submission. In non-AJAX mode, the backend can successfully initiate a siteverify request, which indicates that my Cloudflare secret key configuration, the website server’s outbound internet permissions, and the WordPress network environment are all functioning correctly—it is not a global block or a configuration error. Since Cloudflare reports “Never received a call,” this indicates that in AJAX mode, the WPForms backend handler (or related AJAX routing logic) does not execute the code to send a request to the official Cloudflare API at “https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify” when processing the form, causing the verification to be silently skipped and rendering it ineffective. Version: WPForms 2.0.0.2 WordPress 7.0.4 My Request: Is this a known compatibility bug in WPForms regarding the Turnstile verification module when handling asynchronous AJAX submissions? Does the team have plans to fix this issue? Alternatively, how should we configure WPForms in AJAX mode to force it to perform the siteverify check on the backend? I look forward to your response. Thank you!

support_examples.title: Column names not imported correctly (e.g. itemRestriction → itemReion)
support_examples.description: Replies: 0 Hi there, After exporting a backup with All-in-One WP Migration and importing it into a test environment, I noticed that a column name in the wp_usces_item table (used by the Welcart e-Commerce plugin) had changed like this: itemRestriction → itemReion Has anyone else run into something similar? I’d appreciate any insight if you have. Environment All-in-One WP Migration: 7.110 (started happening right after updating from 7.109) WordPress: 7.1 PHP: 8.3.33 Database: MariaDB 10.5 Welcart e-Commerce: 2.12.1 Something I noticed Looking through the plugin code, there’s a regex in replace_table_options() (in lib/vendor/servmask/database/class-ai1wm-database.php ) that’s meant to strip SQLite’s STRICT table option: '/,?\s*STRICT/i' Since the whitespace before STRICT is optional ( \s* ), it looks like this could also match the “strict” inside a word like Restriction , not just a standalone STRICT keyword — which might explain the column name getting mangled. But I could be wrong about this. If I’m missing something, or if there’s a known workaround, I’d be grateful to hear it. Thanks! This topic was modified 3 days, 17 hours ago by ssssssssss3 .

support_examples.title: rankmath/v1/updateMeta returns 403 rest_forbidden on WooCommerce products
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 Hi Rank Math team, I’m unable to save SEO title/meta description for WooCommerce products through Rank Math’s metabox or the REST route — every save attempt fails silently, and the underlying request returns a 403. Environment: WordPress + WooCommerce + Elementor + Polylang, Rank Math SEO (Free) v1.0.277, hosted on Hostinger. Reproduction: POST /wp-json/rankmath/v1/updateMeta?_locale=user with objectID: 6865, objectType: ‘product’ and real meta content – Logged in as Administrator, valid X-WP-Nonce, valid logged-in cookie – Result: 403 code rest_forbidden, message “Sorry, you are not allowed to do that.” What I’ve already ruled out: User capabilities: confirmed full admin capabilities including manage_options Rank Math Role Manager: all modules enabled for Administrator Custom code snippets (WPCode): reviewed about 20 snippets, none touch REST or capabilities No security or firewall plugin installed LiteSpeed Cache: disabled and retested, same 403 Hosting CDN/WAF (Hostinger): disabled for 5+ minutes and retested, same 403. Hostinger’s own support confirmed via server logs that the request reaches the origin server and the 403 is generated there, not by any edge or CDN layer Core WordPress REST API auth: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users/me with the same nonce and cookies returns 200 with the correct administrator account Core WordPress REST access to the exact same product: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/product/6865 with context=edit, using the same nonce and cookies, also returns 200 successfully A missing wp_rank_math_analytics_objects database table (found in server logs) was recreated via Status and Tools, Database Tools, Re-create Tables. Did not resolve the issue Server logs also show Rank Math making requests to …/rankmath/v1/an/post/undefined, suggesting the product ID is not always reaching the analytics/editor integration correctly Since WordPress core REST auth, cookies, nonce, and capabilities all work correctly for this exact same product, and the CDN/hosting layer is ruled out, this looks like it is coming from inside Rank Math’s own permission_callback for the updateMeta route, or a conflict with WooCommerce/Polylang/Elementor on this specific post type. Could you help identify what that route’s permission_callback checks that core REST doesn’t? Thanks for looking into this.

support_examples.title: Jetpack Wpcom Connection Test returns HTTP 413 and debugger “Unknown error”
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 Hello Jetpack Support Team, I am experiencing a persistent Jetpack connection problem on the following website: Site URL: https://amiratef.com Jetpack version: 16.1.2 WordPress version: 7.1 PHP version: 7.4.33 Web server: LiteSpeed Hosting provider: Namecheap Static shared outbound/public IP: 199.188.200.181 WordPress Site Health reports a critical “Wpcom Connection Test” error. It states that the WordPress.com request is being rejected with HTTP 413. I have completed the following troubleshooting steps: Namecheap whitelisted access to /xmlrpc.php. A GET request to https://amiratef.com/xmlrpc.php now returns HTTP 405 with the expected response: “XML-RPC server accepts POST requests only.” A valid XML-RPC POST request using system.listMethods returns HTTP 200 successfully. Namecheap checked the LiteSpeed and CDN logs and confirmed that there are no blocks on their side. The WordPress memory limit was increased from 64 MB to 128 MB, while WP_MAX_MEMORY_LIMIT remains 256 MB. The issue persisted. ModSecurity was temporarily disabled for testing. The Site Health test still returned HTTP 413, so ModSecurity was re-enabled immediately. The official Jetpack Debug Tool at https://jptools.wordpress.com/debug/ was tested with https://amiratef.com , but it returned: “Unknown error — An unknown error has occurred.” The latest debugger test was performed on August 22, 2026, at approximately 22:24 UTC. The hosting provider has asked me to check whether the static shared IP address 199.188.200.181 is blocked or restricted on the WordPress.com/Jetpack side. Could you please: Check whether 199.188.200.181 is blocked, rate-limited, or restricted by Jetpack/WordPress.com. Check your connection/debugger logs for the request and identify the source of the HTTP 413 response. Confirm which endpoint or request payload is being rejected. Advise what additional diagnostic information is required. No firewall or CDN block was found by the hosting provider, and standard XML-RPC GET and POST tests are currently working. Thank you.

support_examples.title: Fatal error: has_auth() on null crashes all AJAX requests site-wide
support_examples.description: Replies: 4 Hi WPCode team, I’m experiencing a fatal error that crashes every admin-ajax.php request on my site — not just requests related to WPCode, but AJAX calls from other plugins/themes as well (e.g. my theme’s product size guide popup fails with a 500 error because of this). Environment: Plugin: Insert Headers and Footers (WPCode) — latest version WordPress: 7.0.4 PHP: 8.3 Error log: PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to a member function has_auth() on null in /wp-content/plugins/insert-headers-and-footers/includes/lite/admin/notices.php:20 Stack trace: #0 wp-includes/class-wp-hook.php(341): wpcode_maybe_add_library_connect_notice() #1 wp-includes/class-wp-hook.php(365): WP_Hook->apply_filters() #2 wp-includes/plugin.php(522): WP_Hook->do_action() #3 wp-admin/admin-ajax.php(45): do_action() #4 {main} Steps to reproduce: Have WPCode active on a site with any other plugin/theme feature that calls admin-ajax.php (in my case, a WooCommerce product size guide popup from my theme). Trigger that AJAX request on the frontend. Request fails with 500 Internal Server Error. Check debug.log → fatal error shown above. Impact: This breaks unrelated AJAX-based features across the entire site, not just anything related to WPCode. It’s also hard to trace back to WPCode as the root cause since the failure surfaces on completely unrelated frontend features, and only appears in the server error log rather than anywhere visible in the WordPress admin. Happy to provide more details, additional log excerpts, or test on request. Thanks!

support_examples.title: AIOSEO 5.0.1 — dist/Lite/assets/link-format/ ships empty, breaks wpLink
support_examples.description: Replies: 3 AIOSEO 5.0.1 Lite deregisters WordPress core’s wplink script and replaces it with its own build, but that build is missing from the released package. The result is that window.wpLink is never defined, and anything depending on it throws. This is reproducible on every site we updated to 5.0.1 — deactivating AIOSEO resolves it immediately. Error (browser console, on any post edit screen with an ACF link field): Uncaught ReferenceError: wpLink is not defined at acf.Model.open (acf-input.min.js?ver=6.8.8:1:56904) at n.onClickEdit (acf-input.min.js?ver=6.8.8:1:55943) Cause app/Common/Admin/Admin.php:362, in addClassicLinkFormatScript() : wp_deregister_script( 'wplink' ); wp_enqueue_script( 'wplink', aioseo()->core->assets->getAssetsPath( false ) . '/link-format/link-format-classic.js', [ 'jquery', 'wp-a11y' ], aioseo()->version, true); Core wplink is deregistered, then the handle is repointed at link-format-classic.js . In the 5.0.1 package that file does not exist — dist/Lite/assets/link-format/ is an empty directory. The browser 404s on the replacement and, because core’s copy was already deregistered, nothing defines wpLink . Every other asset in dist/Lite/assets/ shipped normally with content hashes ( app.5dbed99e.js , dashboard.e5595a2c.js , etc.), so this looks like the link-format build output was dropped from the release rather than a path bug. The whole bundle appears to be missing, not just the classic file. These are also referenced and also absent: link-format/link-format-classic.js — Admin.php:365 link-format/link-format-block.js — Admin.php:422 link-format/link-format-block-old.js — Admin.php:422 link-format/link-format-block.css — Admin.php:327 So the nofollow / sponsored / UGC link controls should be non-functional in both the Classic and Block editors in this release.

Could you fix the double slash in the enqueue path?

support_examples.title: AIOSEO category sitemap lastmod dates incorrectly show January 1, 1970
support_examples.description: Replies: 3 Hi, I am using All in One SEO v5.0.0.1 and I have found an issue with the category sitemap. Every category in the category sitemap is being given the following last modified date: 1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00 For example, a category URL is output with: 1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00 This affects all categories currently included in the category sitemap. I have carried out a number of checks to rule out an issue with the WordPress database or stale cache. The checks completed are: WordPress wp_posts.post_modified and post_modified_gmt values contain valid recent dates. Posts assigned to the affected categories also have valid modification dates. Category taxonomy records in wp_terms and wp_term_taxonomy appear normal. The affected category terms do not contain unusual data in wp_termmeta . I inspected the wp_aioseo_cache table. The AIOSEO cache entry for aioseo_sitemap_category-sitemap.xml contains "date":"January 1, 1970" . The number of January 1, 1970 values in that cache entry matches the number of categories in the sitemap. I deleted only the category sitemap cache row and then loaded the category sitemap again. AIOSEO regenerated the cache and immediately recreated the same January 1, 1970 dates. I temporarily deactivated all other normal WordPress plugins, leaving AIOSEO active, and the problem remained unchanged. Re-saving the WordPress categories does not resolve the issue. The sitemap is being dynamically regenerated by AIOSEO, so this does not appear to be an old static sitemap file. The underlying WordPress post modification dates are valid, so it appears AIOSEO is calculating or generating the taxonomy/category lastmod value incorrectly and then storing the incorrect January 1, 1970 value in its sitemap cache. Could you please confirm whether this is a known issue with taxonomy/category sitemaps in AIOSEO 5.0.0.1, and whether there is a fix or workaround available? I would prefer not to carry out further invasive troubleshooting on the live site, as the database and underlying WordPress content dates have already been verified as correct. Thanks.

While same address without Port is accepted when CF proxy isn’t active. A better UX would be to prefill the port with the default Varnish port ( 6081 ) in case of Cloudflare/Without Cloudflare, so the field initially contains: 127.0.0.1:6081 The user could then change the port if their Varnish configuration uses a different one. This would also prevent the detection from failing simply because the port was omitted. Thank you.

support_examples.title: AIOS Blocking UptimeRobot Monitoring Requests and Causing UP/DOWN Alerts
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 Hi AIOS Support, We’re experiencing an issue with several WordPress sites where our UptimeRobot monitoring service is intermittently being blocked by AIOS. The sites are only reported as DOWN for a few minutes (10 min max), after which they return to UP. We investigated this with our hosting provider, WP Engine, and they confirmed that there are no server outages or errors during these periods. Our developer determined that when AIOS blocks the monitoring request, it redirects the request to 127.0.0.1 , causing UptimeRobot to report the site as unreachable. Once the block expires, the site returns to normal. We initially found 127.0.0.1 mentioned in the AIOS Country Blocking settings, but Country Blocking is currently disabled. We were advised that the redirect used by 404 detection and the plugin’s block list is separate from that setting. As recommended, we added the UptimeRobot monitoring IP addresses to AIOS → Firewall → Block and Allow Lists → Allow List on a few of the affected sites. Unfortunately, we are still seeing the same UP/DOWN alerts after doing this. We have seen the same behavior on other sites as well. Could you please help us determine what AIOS rule or feature is causing these monitoring requests to be blocked and redirected to 127.0.0.1 ? We’d also appreciate any recommendations for configuring AIOS so that UptimeRobot can reliably monitor the sites without being blocked. Thank you!

support_examples.title: .htaccess, Security Headers failure, WP, AIOS, W3TC plugins
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 I’ve hit a problem with manually editing .htaccess for Security Headers and cannot identify the cause. After loading into my sites, then playing with one site to test this issue, only a couple of the headers are being loaded, in some circumstances, or none, in other circumstances (tests below). I do not know the cause of this so here’s the story so far and how I have experienced this with WordPress (WP), All-In-One-Security (AIOS) plugin and W3 Total Cache (W3TC) plugin. I am including this to all relevant support forums for your information and advice. I know this will probably be something I’ve missed, or it is something buried deep in the system. .htaccess & Security Headers I began by writing the module for several security headers for my sites and adding it to the bottom of my .htaccess file. When exploring the subject I found that AIOS did not currently, directly, support security headers but did have a couple of switches that did present as headers when the site was scanned. These two elements do not appear to be in the .htaccess file section of AIOS code and I assume there are presenting as Headers at a later stage in the page-load process. Test Scanning I used both SecurityHeaders.com and ssl.org to scan. After writing the .htaccess I found the SecurityHeaders reported a “D” rating, showing that only “X-Frame-Options” and “Content-Security-Policy” were detected. Nothing else. W3TC & AIOS After some further, and interesting, exploration I discovered the extensive support page hidden in W3TC for Security Headers (W3TC guys, you really need to tell people about this ) and made selections to match my own coding. AIOS does not, yet, formerly support the full spectrum of Security Headers, but it does include in its Firewall settings the option to block .htaccess editing, plus the switches I mentioned above. Plugin Tests I conducted a series of tests with the two plugins. When I deactivated AIOS the SecurityHeaders.com rating worsened to “F” and no headers were identified. AIOS removed its code from .htaccess when deactivated. Meanwhile W3TC entries in the .htaccess did include my new selections but were not recognised. I also repeated this after clearing caches. No change. “F” rating with no headers being found on both SecurityHeaders.com and ssl.org. Complete failure. No Plugins The next test was to deactivate all plugins. Now the .htaccess was stripped of all AIOS and W3TC coding. Same effect – no security headers were recognised. I even allowed a time delay to allow the deactivation to pass through the server in case that had any effect. It didn’t. HTML Site Test I was concerned that my own code was failing so created a clean .htaccess file into a small HTML site – no WordPress installed. This had no WP coding and nothing from the plugins, just my script. PERFECT RESULT! Both scan sites reported success with the scans, recognised all security headers and it got an “A” rating. So the code is clean, and my Apache server is serving the .htaccess with my edit for successful scanning. WordPress or What? I do not know what else to do with this. Is there something in AIOS or W3TC that is leaving a blockage, code, cache, something in the background that I can’t see, or is this an issue with WP? I’ve tested this repeatedly on a couple of machines and with many edits and reedits of the .htaccess to identify any possible cause, but the same results appear each time. CONCLUSION I’m sharing this experience across the three support forums for WP, AIOS and W3TC in case other people have had similar experiences and to open a broader discussion for all developers. AIOS blocks .htaccess editing, in a limited fashion, W3TC has extensive Security Headers but they’re not recognised, my script works in a clean non-WordPress site. Obviously my thought is that there is a WordPress issue I’ve not rooted out, or there could be a matrix of conflicts in my sites, except the very successful HTML one. Your thoughts are welcome if you feel this is appropriate to your focus: WP, AIOS or W3TC. I will update this as and when I can, but for now I’ve run out of ideas. Can you help? System Used: Apache Server, Latest WP, AIOS & W3TC, Firefox Browsers and Chrome on smartphone for tests.

support_examples.title: Cookie blocker does not block YouTube iframes despite correct configuration
support_examples.description: Replies: 0 Hi, on https://tomoff.de the Complianz cookie blocker does not block YouTube iframes on the front end, although everything appears correctly configured. Consent is opt-in and the region resolves to EU. Environment Complianz GDPR/CCPA 7.5.3.1, WordPress block theme (custom), PHP-FPM on Apache (all-inkl / KAS shared hosting) Active plugins that touch output: WP Rocket 3.21.3 (page cache and minify; lazy load, iframe lazy load and YouTube replacement all OFF, delay JS OFF), EWWW Image Optimizer 8.7.6 (lazy load ON, with youtube in the exclusion list so it does not rewrite the iframes), Wordfence 9.0.0, Rank Math, Burst Statistics, WPCode Lite What is configured Integrations → Services: YouTube is enabled, placeholder enabled Script Center: I added a block rule — URL youtube.com/embed , category Marketing, placeholder enabled, blocked content is an iframe checked, status active Dashboard shows cookie blocker, placeholder and consent banner all green Saved repeatedly ( Settings saved ), settings persist across a full page reload WP Rocket cache purged after every change What happens The delivered HTML contains the unmodified embed: There is no cmplz-blocked-content-container , no cmplz-placeholder , no data-src-cmplz anywhere on the page. The consent banner itself renders correctly and the inline Complianz config reports "consenttype":"optin" and "region":"eu" , so the request is treated as requiring consent. Requests were made with a cache-busting query string, so they are not served from the page cache. Pages to reproduce https://tomoff.de/druck-am-arbeitsplatz-abbauen-7x-konstruktiv-nutzen/ (one embed) https://tomoff.de/wie-treten-sie-ihrer-angst-in-den-hintern/ (two embeds) What I already ruled out Missing blocker CSS (the classes exist and are styled in cookieblocker.min.css ), another plugin rewriting the iframe src before Complianz sees it (fixed — the iframes now carry a real src ), double lazy loading, delayed JavaScript execution, a code snippet disabling the blocker, an allow-list entry, geo-IP misclassification, an inactive service, and unsaved settings. It looks like the cookie blocker’s output filter is not running on the front end at all. What should I check next, and is there a way to verify that the blocker’s output buffer is active? Thanks, Michael

support_examples.title: Issue: notranslate breaks sentence segmentation and removes surrounding spaces
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 I am using the free WordPress version of GTranslate and noticed an issue when class="notranslate" / translate="no" is used inside a sentence. Without notranslate , the sentence is translated correctly. Original HTML Ob variable Messehallen im Grünen, modernes Theaterhaus in der Innenstadt oder historische Klosterkirche direkt am Fluss – in Frankfurt (Oder) finden Sie den passenden Ort für Ihr Event. Result generated by GTranslate Whether variable exhibition halls in the countryside, a modern theater in the city center or a historic monastery church directly on the river – in Frankfurt (Oder) you will find the right place for your event. The visible result is correct: Whether variable exhibition halls in the countryside, a modern theater in the city center or a historic monastery church directly on the river – in Frankfurt (Oder) you will find the right place for your event. Same sentence with notranslate I only exclude the word Messehallen from translation: Ob variable Messehallen im Grünen, modernes Theaterhaus in der Innenstadt oder historische Klosterkirche direkt am Fluss – in Frankfurt (Oder) finden Sie den passenden Ort für Ihr Event. GTranslate then produces: Whether variable Messehallen Whether in the countryside, a modern theater in the city center or a historic monastery church right on the river – in Frankfurt (Oder) you will find the perfect location for your event. The visible result becomes: Whether variableMessehallenWhether in the countryside, a modern theater in the city center or a historic monastery church right on the river – in Frankfurt (Oder) you will find the perfect location for your event. There seem to be two separate problems: The spaces before and after the notranslate element are lost. Expected: variable Messehallen in the countryside Actual: variableMessehallenWhether in the countryside More importantly, the notranslate element appears to split the sentence into separate translation segments. Without notranslate , GTranslate correctly interprets: Ob variable Messehallen im Grünen as one sentence context. With notranslate , the part after the excluded word seems to be translated independently: im Grünen becomes: Whether in the countryside instead of simply: in the countryside So the notranslate span appears to act as a hard translation boundary and causes the surrounding text to lose its original sentence context. I can reproduce this independently of any custom WordPress plugin by inserting the following markup manually into Elementor: Messehallen Therefore, the issue does not seem to be caused by my own implementation. Interestingly, I do not see the same behavior on another website where I use the paid GTranslate version with a similar custom notranslate implementation. The paid version also does not appear to rewrite the translated DOM using the same nested elements. Could you please confirm whether this is a known limitation or bug in the free JavaScript-based version, especially when notranslate is used inside running text? Ideally, excluding a single word or phrase should preserve both: the surrounding whitespace the translation context of the complete sentence This topic was modified 1 day, 14 hours ago by neralex .

wordpress.name: WooCommerce PayPal Payments

review_examples.title: Months of payment problems, extensive testing, and still no clear solution (2 stars)
review_examples.description: Replies: 2 Rating: 2 stars I initially had a positive experience with the WooCommerce PayPal Payments plugin and its support, which is why I previously left a positive review. Unfortunately, my experience changed significantly following a series of payment and checkout problems that began in late 2025. Around October 2025, my business revenue began falling dramatically. At first, I could not establish whether this was simply a business or marketing issue, or whether there was a problem with the payment system. I contacted Syde, the developers and support team behind the plugin, and was advised to update to the latest version of the plugin. I did so. Business improved somewhat, but revenue remained substantially below the levels I would normally expect. January is historically one of the strongest months of the year for my business. Instead, January was disastrous. This prompted me to look much more closely at the WooCommerce and payment logs. What I found was alarming. For a period of time, almost every credit-card payment attempt appeared to be failing. I raised this with support and was largely told that the problem was occurring on the customer’s bank or card-issuer side, with explanations such as declined transactions or suspected fraud. However, after approximately two months, the number of failed card payments dropped dramatically without any clear change that explained why. This made me question whether the explanation that the banks were primarily responsible had ever fully explained what I was seeing. Business nevertheless remained weak, which led me to investigate the PayPal payment flow more closely. One particularly confusing issue occurred when I opened the Basket page on my mobile phone and noticed messaging within the PayPal payment flow suggesting that the customer might need to pay significantly more than the displayed course price because of possible shipping and tax adjustments. My courses are digital products and I do not charge shipping. I asked Syde to explain this. Initially, I was told that the figure was related to PayPal Pay Later messaging. However, this explanation did not appear to match what I was actually seeing or how the payment flow was behaving. After further discussion, the issue appeared to be connected to the configuration of the payment and shipping flow rather than simply being a Pay Later calculation. I was eventually able to improve this part of the customer journey by enabling Pay Now Experience. However, changing settings in order to solve one problem appeared to introduce further questions and trade-offs. In my case, for example, the Basket Smart Button flow allows customers to complete payment without going through the same account-registration process as the standard Checkout flow. I repeatedly asked Syde to review my complete WooCommerce and PayPal configuration to make sure there were no conflicting or inappropriate settings. I was told that testing and checks had been carried out, but the subsequent discoveries made me question whether the full payment flow had actually been investigated thoroughly from the beginning. The plugin has a large number of settings and interactions involving WooCommerce checkout, PayPal buttons, shipping, digital products, account creation, Pay Now Experience, 3D Secure and other payment options. I do not expect every merchant to be an expert in these technical details. That is precisely why effective technical support is important. To be fair, Syde generally responded to my emails within their stated response timeframe. The problem, in my experience, was not simply the speed of replies. The problem was that, for many months, the replies did not produce a clear diagnosis or solution. I often felt that I was being required to carry out the investigation myself: checking logs, testing different settings, changing configurations, monitoring transactions and repeatedly reporting the results. The situation only appeared to change significantly after I made it clear that I was considering changing to another PayPal plugin and revising my previous positive review. At that point, Syde finally carried out more extensive testing and acknowledged that there was a genuine problem with the mobile checkout flow. They were able to reproduce a checkout validation issue on Android devices. However, my own subsequent testing showed that the issue was not confined to Android. I spent approximately four hours systematically testing the staging site using Safari and Chrome in private/incognito mode, on both desktop and iPhone. The results were inconsistent and concerning. On desktop, the PayPal and card payment flows generally completed successfully and displayed the expected Order Received confirmation. On mobile, however, I reproduced several problems: • Safari on iOS: PayPal payment through the Checkout page returned to the Checkout form and asked the customer to complete the details again, creating a payment loop instead of reaching the Order Received page. • Chrome on iOS: a PayPal payment through the Checkout page could be successfully completed, but the customer was then returned to the Checkout form rather than being shown the Order Received confirmation. • Chrome on iOS: a PayPal payment from the Basket could be successfully processed, but the customer was returned to the Basket page without an Order Received confirmation or notification. • Card payments through the Checkout page worked correctly on mobile during my testing. These findings are particularly concerning because, in some scenarios, the payment itself was successful but the customer was not shown a clear confirmation page. From the customer’s perspective, it could appear that the payment had failed, potentially encouraging them to try again. There were also differences in the availability of guest card payment through PayPal between desktop and mobile testing. On desktop, I was able to see an option allowing payment without creating a PayPal account. On mobile, that option was not consistently available. I appreciate that software bugs can occur and that reproducing a problem across different devices and configurations can sometimes be difficult. My criticism is not that a bug exists. My criticism is the amount of time it took before the existence of a genuine problem was acknowledged and properly investigated. I began raising concerns many months ago after seeing a dramatic and sustained decline in revenue and unusual payment behaviour. I repeatedly provided logs, descriptions, URLs, settings and test results. For a long time, the explanations focused on external factors such as customers’ banks or card issuers. Only after extensive persistence, repeated testing and the possibility that I might move to a competing plugin did the investigation appear to become sufficiently thorough. I have also since read other user reviews and found reports from users describing payment, checkout and support problems that appear similar in nature to some of the difficulties I have experienced. That further reduced my confidence that my experience was simply an isolated problem. My business has almost certainly lost sales during this period. I cannot quantify precisely how many, or attribute every lost sale solely to this plugin, but when a business experiences a major revenue decline at the same time as significant payment failures and inconsistent checkout behaviour, it is impossible to ignore the possibility that the payment system has contributed to the problem. At the time of writing, Syde’s team has acknowledged at least one genuine mobile checkout issue and says that the matter is under investigation. I hope they find and fix the underlying cause. I would prefer to continue using the plugin and to update this review positively if the problems are properly resolved. However, after spending months trying to understand these issues—and many additional hours personally testing payment flows—I need a reliable payment system that works consistently across desktop and mobile devices. If a clear and reliable solution is not provided, I will have little choice but to move to an alternative PayPal integration and update this review to reflect my full experience. My advice to other merchants is to test every payment flow yourself, particularly: desktop and mobile; PayPal and card payments; Basket Smart Buttons and Checkout buttons; guest checkout; successful payment redirects and Order Received confirmations. Do not assume that a successful payment alone means that the customer’s checkout experience has completed correctly.

support_examples.title: Subtotal mismatch triggers PAYER_ACTION_REQUIRED and a duplicate cancelled order
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 Environment WooCommerce PayPal Payments: 4.1.2 WooCommerce: 11.0.1 WordPress: 7.1 PHP: 8.3.33 Currency: EUR — prices include VAT (7%), i.e. tax-inclusive pricing Settings already in place Subtotal Mismatch Behavior: “Add another line item” WooCommerce → Settings → Tax → “Round tax at subtotal level”: enabled Plugin updated to the latest version Problem On some orders we get two WooCommerce orders for a single checkout: one is paid successfully, and a second, duplicate order is left unpaid and ends up “Cancelled”. The money is captured correctly and only once, so this is not a payment/settlement problem — it’s a duplicate order being created and then auto-cancelled, which is confusing for us and our accounting. What the PayPal log shows (one representative case) PayPal order created with amount 127.05 (item_total 118.74, tax 8.31). Buyer approves — CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED. Plugin PATCHes the order: amount changed to 127.06 (tax 8.31 → 8.32) and a “Subtotal mismatch” line item of 0.02 is added. (The three product unit amounts sum to 118.72, but item_total is reported as 118.74.) First capture attempt fails: UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY / PAYER_ACTION_REQUIRED — “Failed to capture order.” Buyer approves a second time; log shows “WC order XXXXX has been processed after approval in PayPal.” PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED for 127.06 — money captured once, correctly. WARNING: “Could not process PayPal completed order #[PayPal order ID], Status: COMPLETED.” The next order number is the duplicate, and it gets cancelled. Our understanding The subtotal correction / amount change is applied AFTER the buyer has already approved the PayPal order. Changing the amount post-approval invalidates the approval (PAYER_ACTION_REQUIRED), which forces a re-approval and appears to result in the duplicate order that then cancels. Questions Is this expected behaviour with “Add another line item”? Will switching to “Do not send line items to PayPal” reliably prevent the post-approval amount change, and therefore the duplicate/cancelled order? Is there any way to make the subtotal reconciliation happen BEFORE buyer approval rather than after? Is the €0.02 discrepancy (unit amounts summing to 118.72 vs item_total 118.74) a known rounding issue with tax-inclusive EUR pricing, and is there a recommended configuration for this case? I can provide a full sanitised log excerpt if that helps.

support_examples.title: Bug report: Card Payments “Place Order” hangs forever
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 Summary When a customer selects “Debit & Credit Cards” at checkout, fills in valid card details, and clicks “Place Order,” the button greys out and the page shows a permanent loading overlay. It never resolves — no error, no redirect, nothing. The customer is stuck and has to abandon the purchase. I lost a real sale to this before tracking it down. Steps to reproduce Add a product to the cart and go to /checkout/ (classic/shortcode checkout via [woocommerce_checkout] , not WooCommerce Blocks). Fill in billing details. Select “DEBIT & CREDIT CARDS.” Enter a valid-format test card number, expiry, and CVV. Check the terms and conditions box. Click “PLACE ORDER.” Expected behavior Either the order processes (redirect / success) or a clear validation/decline message appears. Actual behavior The “Place Order” button greys out and a permanent loading overlay (jQuery blockUI) appears and never clears. Confirmed via browser devtools that after clicking Place Order: Zero network requests are made to any paypal.com domain. Zero requests are made to the site’s own wc-ajax=checkout endpoint. jQuery.active returns 0 (no pending AJAX). No JavaScript errors appear in the console. In other words, the click on “Place Order” never seems to reach PayPal’s card tokenization flow at all — it just hangs indefinitely with no network activity and no error. What I’ve already ruled out Caching/JS delay : Fully disabled WP Rocket’s “Delay JavaScript execution” for the checkout page specifically (not just excluded PayPal scripts — turned the feature off entirely for this page) and cleared cache. No change. Plugin conflicts : Deactivated WooCommerce Payments (Stripe) entirely, in case its dormant JS was conflicting. No change. Cache staleness : Cleared WP Rocket cache (site-wide “Clear and Preload”) between every test. Toggling the setting : Disabled “Advanced Credit and Debit Card Payments,” saved, re-enabled, saved, cleared cache, retested. Same result every time. Some diagnostics that might help narrow it down The PayPal JS SDK script tag on the checkout page requests components=buttons,funding-eligibility,messages,card-fields — so card-fields is being loaded correctly (not the older hosted-fields ), and window.paypal.CardFields is present in the browser. So the SDK side looks correctly configured. Given that, the click on “Place Order” apparently isn’t reaching (or isn’t successfully triggering) the CardFields renderer’s submit/tokenization handler — nothing is ever sent to PayPal, and nothing is sent to WooCommerce’s own checkout endpoint either. This is a classic (shortcode) checkout, not WooCommerce Blocks checkout, built on Elementor’s “Hello Elementor” theme. Environment WordPress: 7.1 WooCommerce: 11.0.1 WooCommerce PayPal Payments: 4.1.2 Theme: Hello Elementor (child theme), Classic theme type Elementor: 4.2.3 / Elementor Pro: 4.2.2 Checkout type: Classic checkout ( [woocommerce_checkout] shortcode) Caching: WP Rocket 3.23.3.3 (Delay JS execution disabled on the checkout page specifically; confirmed not the cause) PHP: 8.3.33 PayPal Payments status report shows: Onboarded ✓, Currency supported ✓, Advanced Card Processing available in country ✓, Webhook status ✓ — no eligibility warnings shown. Shop country: GB, currency: GBP Additional context I found several similar reports (some closed without visible resolution details, some resolved by PayPal support directly patching the plugin within a day or two): GitHub issues #4259, #2099, #2806, #1464, #3634, and WordPress.org threads including “Advanced Credit/Debit Card not working without Paypal Enabled” and “PayPal’s Advanced Card Processing Stopped Working” — the latter was traced by your team to Advanced Card Processing depending on Smart Button Locations being enabled on the checkout page, though that doesn’t appear to apply here since PayPal’s own smart buttons do render correctly on this checkout page (the standard “PayPal” option works fine — this issue is specific to the “Debit & Credit Cards” option only). I’ve currently had to disable “Advanced Credit and Debit Card Payments” entirely on the live site because of this — customers can currently only pay via Trustly or PayPal, not by card directly, which is hurting conversions. Would really appreciate a look at this, and happy to provide site access or further logs/HAR files if useful. Thank you!

review_examples.title: Great for Merchant Center feeds, but conversion tracking creates conflicts with (1 star)
review_examples.description: Replies: 5 Rating: 1 star I’ve spent several weeks testing this plugin on a live WooCommerce store together with Google Ads, Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager. The plugin does an excellent job syncing products with Google Merchant Center and generating the product feed. Unfortunately, the tracking side of the plugin causes several problems. Here are the main issues I encountered: The plugin automatically creates Google Ads conversion actions after connecting an existing Google Ads account, even when I explicitly selected that I already have campaigns and an existing tracking setup. During the campaign creation process, it immediately tries to create Google Ads campaigns instead of simply allowing Merchant Center synchronization and statistics. Purchase tracking appears to be sent automatically by the plugin, even when I use Google Tag Manager (GTM4WP) as my only tracking solution. There is no clear option to completely disable all conversion tracking while keeping only the product feed functionality. Even with Enhanced Conversions disabled inside the plugin, purchase-related data still appears to be transmitted, making it difficult to understand which source is sending conversions. The automatically generated conversion actions create conflicts with existing GTM implementations and can result in duplicate purchase events or very difficult debugging. The plugin mixes Merchant Center, Google Ads tracking and campaign management into one package. Many advanced users only need Merchant Center synchronization and product feeds. My current setup is: WooCommerce Google Tag Manager (GTM4WP) Google Analytics 4 Google Ads conversion tracking through GTM Google Merchant Center In this setup I want GTM to be the only source of conversion tracking, while the plugin should only manage the product feed. Suggestions: Add a “Feed Only” mode. Allow disabling all Google Ads conversion tracking. Do not automatically create Google Ads conversion actions. Do not automatically create campaigns unless the user explicitly requests it. Separate Merchant Center functionality from Google Ads tracking. Provide clearer documentation about which events are sent automatically and how to disable them. The feed functionality is very good, but the automatic tracking behavior makes the plugin difficult to use together with professional GTM implementations.

support_examples.title: Currency selection conflict even when the multi-currency feature is disabled
support_examples.description: Replies: 6 Several of my clients, who use the multi-currency plugin I developed (Aelia Currency Switcher) have reported an issue that started occurring with the latest version of Woo Payments (11.0). The Currency Switcher handles all the multi-currency aspect, as it always did, therefore the multi-currency features in the Woo Payments plugin must be disabled, to prevent conflicts (double conversions, currency selection, and so on). This has been working fine until recently. The latest version of the Woo Payments plugin has introduced a bug that causes the active currency to be replaced by the shop’s base currency, even when the multi-currency features of Woo Payments are disabled. How the currency selection normally works: A shop has multiple currencies, such as EUR (base currency), USD, GBP. A visitor chooses a currency, e.g. USD. The active currency becomes USD. The price of Product A is converted from 100 EUR to 117.07 USD. The checkout shows 117.07 USD. The customer completes the purchase via Woo Payments and pays 117.07 USD. This was working fine until a few weeks ago. Starting from version 11.0 of Woo Payments, the following is happening: A shop has multiple currencies, such as EUR (base currency), USD, GBP. A visitor chooses a currency, e.g. USD. The active currency becomes USD. The price of Product A is converted from 100 EUR to 117.07 USD. Woo Payments replaces the active currency with EUR. The checkout shows 117.07 EUR . The customer completes the purchase via Woo Payments and pays 117.07 EUR . I haven’t been able to reproduce the same issue on a test server, but this has been reported by several different clients, all of whom were using Woo Payments 11.0. Disabling that plugin restores the normal behaviour. I also asked them to try installing an earlier version, to see if that makes a difference, and I’m waiting for their feedback. Please note that this issue occurs even if Woo Payments is installed, but not configured or actually used for payments . In some cases, the plugin was “sitting there”, its settings page waiting at “start configuration”, so not in a usable state. Somehow, it’s multi-currency code kicks in from the moment it’s activated. Expected behaviour Woo Payments should not affect the active currency when its multi-currency features are disabled. Update – Fresh from the press (12:15 CEST) One of the clients switched to Woo Payments 10.9 and the issue disappeared. The fronted works fine, the prices are correct and payments now go through in the correct currency, also using Woo Payments. This should confirm that the conflict has been inadvertently introduced in Woo Payments 11.0. This topic was modified 1 week, 2 days ago by Diego .

review_examples.title: Critical Warning: Failed on All Core Function (5 stars)
review_examples.description: Replies: 1 Rating: 5 stars I am writing this review to save other developers and site owners the immense amount of time I have just lost. I needed to implement standard GA4 e-commerce tracking on a professional WordPress/WooCommerce site. Based on its popularity and countless recommendations, I chose GTM4WP as the solution to generate the required dataLayer. Unfortunately, after days of intensive, professional-level debugging, I discovered that the plugin was completely non-functional in my specific—yet very common—environment. The plugin failed at its two most essential tasks: GTM Snippet Injection: The plugin’s most basic feature—injecting the GTM container script into the website’s and —did not work at all. The script was simply not present. I had to bypass this functionality entirely and inject the code manually using another method (Code Snippets) just to get our GTM container to load. E-commerce dataLayer Generation (The Deal-Breaker): This is the primary reason anyone uses this plugin. After successfully loading our GTM container manually, I ran a full test purchase. By analyzing the GTM debug mode and the site’s dataLayer object, I can confirm that GTM4WP completely failed to generate the purchase event and its corresponding ecommerce object on the WooCommerce order confirmation page. It produced absolutely nothing. My Technical Environment (Please read this before you install): To help others, here is the stack where the plugin failed. This is likely the source of the conflict: CMS: WordPress E-commerce: WooCommerce Theme: Hello Elementor (using a child theme) Page Builder: Elementor Pro Key Detail: I am using Elementor Pro to customize the WooCommerce page templates, including the “Thank You” / “Order Received” page. Conclusion: My conclusion is that GTM4WP is fundamentally incompatible with themes or page builders that override default WooCommerce templates—a standard practice for virtually any custom-designed website today. Because it cannot handle this common scenario, the plugin proved to be entirely useless for my project. While it may work on simple sites with basic, unmodified themes, it is not a reliable solution for professional, customized builds. The time and effort wasted diagnosing this incompatibility were substantial. I cannot recommend this plugin and strongly advise users with a similar tech stack to seek a manual implementation from the start.

support_examples.description: Replies: 1 Subject: Fatal error: memory exhausted in integration/woocommerce.php line 1015 – repeated checkout crashes Hello, We’re experiencing a critical issue with GTM4WP (Google Tag Manager for WordPress) on our WooCommerce store, causing repeated HTTP 500 errors on our checkout page. Error (from server logs): PHP Fatal error: Allowed memory size of 1073741824 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 262144 bytes) in /wp-content/plugins/duracelltomi-google-tag-manager/integration/woocommerce.php on line 1015 This is immediately followed by: PHP Fatal error: Allowed memory size of 1073741824 bytes exhausted in /wp-includes/class-wp-fatal-error-handler.php on line 37 Context: The error occurs consistently on /checkout/ and occasionally on /cart/ PHP memory limit is already set to 1024MB, which should be more than sufficient for a standard WooCommerce checkout Our store has a large product catalog with many variations (size/color combinations) We use several WooCommerce extensions that modify product/pricing data: WooCommerce, Flux Checkout, Woo Discount Rules (+ Pro), YITH Advanced Refund System, FOX Currency Switcher, WCBoost Variation Swatches, Order Minimum/Maximum Amount Limits We had the “Fire view_item on parent product” setting enabled in GTM4WP’s WooCommerce integration; disabling this setting alone did not resolve the issue The site runs WordPress 7.0.2, WooCommerce 10.9.4, PHP 8.2.32, on Ubuntu 22.04 with Nginx as reverse proxy in front of Apache/PHP-FPM Current status: We’ve had to deactivate GTM4WP entirely to restore checkout functionality, as this was blocking customer orders. Question: Is this a known issue with large product catalogs or many variations? Could the WooCommerce Data Layer integration be looping or serializing an excessively large object (e.g., all product variations) rather than just the cart contents? Any guidance on a fix, workaround, or plugin update that addresses this would be greatly appreciated, as we need e-commerce tracking (GA4 conversions, Google Ads remarketing) back in place as soon as possible. support_examples.title: Critical Error Logs
support_examples.description: Replies: 3 When attempting to access TablePress from the WP dashboard, we get a critical error that prevents the plugin from loading. After some investigation, we found the following support thread, which appears to describe a similar issue: https://wordpress.org/support/topic/critical-error-logs-related-to-tablepress-plugin/ We also came across the following guidance related to the Freemius SDK: “If you are using the licensing methods is_plan() or is_plan__premium_only() in your integration with the WP SDK, then transition to the is_plan_or_trial() and is_plan_or_trial__premium_only() methods accordingly.” The errors we’re seeing indicate that Tablepress is attempting to call methods that are not available in our environment. For example: PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined method class@anonymous::pricing_url() …/wp-content/plugins/tablepress/classes/class-view.php:411 PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined method class@anonymous::is_plan_or_trial__premium_only() …/wp-content/plugins/tablepress/views/view-edit.php:346 As a temporary workaround, we manually modified classes/class-view.php and views/view-edit.php to bypass these function calls, which allows TablePress to load successfully. These changes are overwritten each time the plugin is updated, which has been requiring us to reapply the changes after every update. One possibility we considered is that this may be related to the bundled Freemius SDK. TablePress 3.3.2 appears to include Freemius 2.13.1, and because the fatal errors involve Freemius-related methods (pricing_url() and is_plan_or_trial__premium_only()), we’re wondering if there could be an issue with the SDK integration or initialization. We haven’t been able to confirm that’s the cause, but wanted to mention it in case it’s helpful for troubleshooting. Would you be willing to help us determine whether this is a known issue or whether there’s another underlying cause? We’d be happy to provide any additional logs, environment details, or other information that would assist with diagnosing the problem. We are on 3.3.4 and this issue has affected us for quite a while. We have a multi site configuration in case that is helpful info.

support_examples.title: please remove forminator classes or allow override
support_examples.description: Replies: 3 For people using gutenberg and other default global styles, there is no simple way to make forminator forms inherit the button styles. for example, if i turn off forminator styling and use basic option or none, the button shows as plain html button. it will not inherit the global button styles for the site. your none option removes the styling but does not remove your classes or allow them to be replaced at the form/plugin level as other plugins do. example: https://www.billerickson.net/wpforms-submit-button-match-gutenberg-button-style/ please change your plugin to not output css classes for forminator if people set to none and want to inherit all their global styles. other plugins allow users to simply replace the class on an element with the global class name at the plugin level: “wp-block-button__link wp-element-button” thanks! i love this plugin but this aspect makes it very outdated and not up to FSE block theming standards for 2026 and beyond. if anyone else finds this thread, here’s a functions.php solution gemini made that strips the forminator class and replaces with the default global styles: /** * Replace Forminator submit button classes with Gutenberg global style classes. */ add_filter( 'forminator_render_button_markup', 'inherit_gutenberg_button_classes_in_forminator', 10, 2 ); function inherit_gutenberg_button_classes_in_forminator( $html, $button ) { // 1. Ensure we only target the submit button if ( strpos( $html, 'forminator-button-submit' ) !== false ) { // 2. Replace Forminator's submit button element wrapper with Gutenberg's button block wrapper $html = str_replace( 'forminator-field', 'forminator-field wp-block-button', $html ); // 3. Replace the native Forminator button classes with Gutenberg block button classes $html = str_replace( 'class="forminator-button forminator-button-submit"', 'class="wp-block-button__link wp-element-button forminator-button-submit"', $html ); } return $html; }

support_examples.title: Email to Admin has address problem
support_examples.description: Replies: 0 Some time ago, we set the Ninja Form fields, for the email that goes to the viewer, with From Name and From Email being the specific name and email of the admin person who receives the submission. Now, we have the problem that while the form is correctly set up to pick up the field values entered by the viewer, the email server is sending them using their own address in the header, which is different from the address used by the viewer. This is causing a fail on the send. The following is what my client’s email host is saying about it. “The problem is that the form is setting a header from of whatever email address is put into the email field on the contact us form. That results in the header being from one address and the SMTP (envelope) being from another. This results in the email being blocked for that reason and because the server that relays the email does not have permission to relay for those addresses 90% of the time.” Is this something that has a solution on your end, or should it be handled on the web host end? support_examples.description: Replies: 2 Environment: WordPress 7.0.3, WPML 4.9.6 + WPML Media Translation 3.1.2 (three active languages, media duplicated to translations), Enable Media Replace 4.2.2 Steps: Upload an image. WPML creates three attachment posts, one per language, all sharing one _wp_attached_file value and one physical file. Switch admin language to any one of them, open that sibling. Replace media → “Replace the file, use the new file name, and update all links” → upload a differently named file. Expected: all siblings follow the replacement, or the old file is retained while other posts still reference it. Actual: only the invoked sibling is repointed. The old full-size file is deleted while two other attachment posts still reference it. Both remaining languages 404 on full size. Cause: classes/Controller/ReplaceController.php:504 calls @unlink($attached_file) directly. This bypasses the wp_delete_file filter, which WPML uses in WPML_Attachment_Action::delete_file_filter() to block deletion of files still referenced by sibling attachments. EMR’s own sub-size deletion in classes/compat.php does use wp_delete_file_from_directory() and is correctly blocked, which is why the thumbnails survive and the loss goes unnoticed. Impact: irreversible loss of original media, silent because admin thumbnails continue to render. Happy to provide additional information if needed.

support_examples.title: Bug report: Uncaught `ResolutionOversizeException`
support_examples.description: Replies: 3 # Bug report: Uncaught ResolutionOversizeException causes a fatal error (HTTP 500) ** Plugin: ** WebP Converter for Media ** Version: ** 6.6.2 and 6.6.3 (still present in the latest release) ** Environment: ** WordPress 7.0.2 / PHP 8.5.5 (fpm-fcgi) / conversion method: GD (bundled 2.1.0), shared hosting --- ## Summary GdMethod::convert_image_to_output() throws ResolutionOversizeException for images larger than 8192px, but no catch block anywhere in the plugin handles it. The exception escapes as a fatal error, so a single oversized image in the Media Library breaks conversion entirely. ## What happens Running a bulk regeneration from the settings screen returns: 500 - (https://example.com/wp-json/webp-converter/v1/regenerate/) The REST response carries no message, so the cause is invisible from the admin UI. Running the plugin's own WP-CLI command reveals it: PHP Fatal error: Uncaught WebpConverter\Exception\ResolutionOversizeException: Image is larger than maximum 8K resolution: ".../uploads/2024/05/example.jpg" in .../src/Conversion/Method/GdMethod.php:200 ## Root cause src/Conversion/Method/GdMethod.php:199-200 php } elseif ( ( imagesx( $image ) > 8192 ) || ( imagesy( $image ) > 8192 ) ) { throw new ResolutionOversizeException( $source_path ); src/Conversion/Method/LibraryMethodAbstract.php:54-61 — the only catch on this path: php } catch ( OutputPathException $e ) { $this->save_conversion_error( $e->getMessage(), $plugin_settings ); } catch ( SourcePathException|FilesizeOversizeException|ImageInvalidException $e ) { $this->save_conversion_error( $e->getMessage(), $plugin_settings ); $this->skip_crashed->create_crashed_file( $output_path ); } catch ( LargerThanOriginalException $e ) { return; } ResolutionOversizeException is not listed. All exception classes extend ExceptionAbstract directly (a flat hierarchy), so it is not caught by inheritance either, and there is no catch higher up the stack — MethodIntegrator::convert_paths() does not wrap the call. Every other "skip this file" condition degrades gracefully into a warning. This one does not. ## The same gap affects other exceptions on this path Found by inspection, not reproduced — but they are thrown inside the same try and are equally absent from the catch list: | Exception | Thrown at | Trigger | |---|---|---| | ResolutionOversizeException | GdMethod.php:200 | image over 8192px ** (reproduced) ** | | ImageAnimatedException | GdMethod.php:91 | animated GIF | | ConversionErrorException | GdMethod.php:202 , ImagickMethod.php:165 | encoder failure | | FunctionUnavailableException | GdMethod.php:99,154,159,167,172,198 | missing GD function | | ExtensionUnsupportedException | GdMethod.php:106 , ImagickMethod.php:92 | unsupported extension | | ImagickUnavailableException | ImagickMethod.php:90 | Imagick missing | | ImagickNotSupportWebpException | ImagickMethod.php:146 | Imagick without WebP | Notably, GdMethod::convert_image_to_output() documents @throws ConversionErrorException , @throws FunctionUnavailableException and @throws ResolutionOversizeException , yet none of the three is caught. ## Why there is no user-side workaround Switching to Imagick would avoid GD's 8192px limit, but on this server Imagick::queryformats( 'WEBP' ) returns an empty array (ImageMagick 6.9.10-68 built without WebP), so ImagickMethod::is_method_active() returns false and the plugin correctly disables that option. On shared hosting ImageMagick cannot be rebuilt. So on any server with GD-only WebP support, one oversized image makes the endpoint return 500 with no way to recover from the settings screen. We are currently patching the plugin file after every update, which is obviously not sustainable. ## Suggested fix Minimal — add the exception to the existing clause: php } catch ( SourcePathException|FilesizeOversizeException|ImageInvalidException|ResolutionOversizeException $e ) { Preferable — catch the whole family, which is what RemoteMethod.php:130 already does: php } catch ( ExceptionInterface $e ) { $this->save_conversion_error( $e->getMessage(), $plugin_settings ); } Since every plugin exception implements ExceptionInterface and each one represents a recoverable "skip this file" condition, catching the interface in LibraryMethodAbstract would close this class of bug for good rather than one exception at a time — and would make LibraryMethodAbstract consistent with RemoteMethod . ## Verification After adding ResolutionOversizeException to the catch clause, the same run completes normally: Warning: Image is larger than maximum 8K resolution: ".../example.jpg" Success: ... Converted files: 2 Failed or skipped: 1 EXIT=0 The oversized file is skipped with a warning, and the remaining images convert as expected. Thank you for the plugin — and for the quick CURLINFO_SIZE_DOWNLOAD_T fix in 6.6.3.

support_examples.title: Issue with product description in woocommerce product pages
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 Subject: SureForms causes malformed HTML nesting on WooCommerce product pages (Divi 5) — even though no SureForms form is present on those pages Hello, I’m running into a layout bug on WooCommerce product pages built with Divi 5 Theme Builder, and Elegant Themes’ support team has confirmed that disabling SureForms fixes it. This is puzzling because the affected product pages don’t contain any SureForms form — I only have 2 forms on the whole site, both on unrelated pages (not product pages). What I can confirm precisely (I inspected the raw HTML via “View Page Source”, not the browser’s auto-corrected DOM inspector, so this reflects the actual server response): On affected product pages, a Divi Theme Builder row contains two columns: one with the “Woo Product Description” module, one with the “Woo Product Image” module. They should sit side by side. Instead, the image column renders below, full width. Counting the raw HTML tags precisely shows the row’s own wrapping gets closed one level too early — right after the description module’s content, before the sibling image column is output — which ejects the image column out of the row. There’s also a stray orphan closing tag appended right after the last real paragraph of the description (no matching opening ). This happens consistently regardless of the actual description text, on every variable product using this specific module/row combination — but ONLY when SureForms is active, on pages that don’t use SureForms at all. Could you help me understand what SureForms loads or modifies on every front-end page load, regardless of whether a form is present? Specifically: Does SureForms enqueue any global CSS/JS on all pages, or only on pages containing a form block/shortcode? Does SureForms hook into any global output filter (e.g., the_content, template_redirect, output buffering, HTML minification/optimization) that runs site-wide? Is there a setting to restrict SureForms’ assets/processing to only the pages where a form is actually embedded? Environment: SureForms version: lastest Divi version: lastest WordPress version: lastest Affected page example: https://diviso.jardindeveil.net/produit/coffret-solides-de-platon-blanc-couleur-o40-mm-avec-boussole/ Happy to provide a full HTML export of the broken section, or test with debugging enabled, if that helps narrow this down. Thank you.
