support_examples.description: Replies: 2 Environment * WordPress (latest version) * Astra Theme * SureForms * WP Mail SMTP * XServer hosting * Custom domain email configured Issue When the contact form is submitted: * Admin notification email is sent successfully. * Form submission is saved correctly in Entries. * The submitter’s email address is stored correctly in Entries. However, * User Auto Reply notification is not sent. WP Mail SMTP debug log records the following error: “You must provide at least one recipient email address.” What I have already confirmed 1. Form submission works correctly. 2. The user’s email address is stored correctly in Entries. 3. Admin notification emails are delivered successfully. 4. WP Mail SMTP is working properly. 5. User Auto Reply notification is enabled. 6. Send Email To is set to {user_email}. 7. “User Email” appears in the notification tag selector. 8. The email field is required. 9. The email field slug is “enter-email-address”. 10. Conditional Logic is disabled. Steps to reproduce 1. Enter name, email address, and message in the contact form. 2. Submit the form. 3. Admin notification email is received successfully. 4. Submission data is saved in Entries. 5. User Auto Reply email is not delivered. 6. WP Mail SMTP logs the error: “You must provide at least one recipient email address.” Additional Information The sender’s email address is correctly stored in Entries, so it does not appear that SureForms is failing to collect the email address from the form. support_examples.title: Feedback and suggestion (v4 was better than v5)
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 Feedback and a suggestion Feedback: I used v4 for years no issues, but I cannot use v5. Not sure if it is down to wp-cron not working although I have even moved my site to 3 hosts since v5 launched and backwpup never worked on any of them. Not manual or automatic (not that I really care about automatic), and doesn’t matter where I tried to save the backup to, webhost or external such as dropbox, it just does not work. You cannot just download a backup with one click like you used to and it seems to more rely on the server features now than just being able to backup when you want. Why can’t we have the basic feature that was in v4 where you clicked backup and it gave you a backup? That version didn’t care about wp-cron or scheduled tasks. You could just backup and save the backup. Why can’t we do that on v5? I try out v5 on each webhost but it never works no matter where I try to save the backup to, plus as I said, you can’t just download a backup and be done with it like you used to be able to do. This is why I still use v4 as v5 just doesn’t work and as I said, not sure if it is down to webhost and the server, but it never used to matter and it used to work on any webhost, but v5 doesn’t. It doesn’t tell me why it won’t backup, it just doesn’t do it no matter where I set the backup to be saved. External, internal, doesn’t matter, it doesn’t work. The only error I ever see is about wp-cron so I assume that is why it doesn’t work. I am not here to troubleshoot why its not working as I tried that back when you launched v5 ( I made a post back then trying to sort it but it never works and the debug log was useless as it was blank every time ), plus I am chronically ill and have spent way too many hours trying to get it work or to get the debug log to show why its not working but it never actually showed what was wrong so I never got anywhere trying to figure out why it doesn’t work, but I can only assume its related to wp-cron. Lots of other people have the exact same issue and either use v4 or use a different plugin now, so I know I am not the only one. So I am just trying to give feedback and a suggestion to get the basic v4 feature added to v5 where you could just download a backup and it would do it. That version didn’t care about your webhost or server, it just gave you the backup you wanted there and then. We didn’t need to have certain webhost/server features to use v4 to backup, so would be nice if we didn’t need anything for the v5. It just did the job and gave you a file to save. Why can’t that be added to v5? I use v4 still as that is my only option or it won’t work, but would be nice if we could all just use v5 and have the exact same feature in v5 for those that want it as a lot still use v4. Suggestion: PLEASE add the v4 feature where you could just download it straight away, not saved to your webhost or whatever, just a option to download a backup there and then like you can in v4.

wordpress.name: Meta for WooCommerce

review_examples.title: Caused multiple site crashes (1 star)
review_examples.description: Replies: 1 Rating: 1 star Not built with the performance or stability of larger WooCommerce stores in mind whatsoever. We ran this on a dedicated VPS with 8 CPU cores and 24 GB RAM, and its catalogue/feed syncing brought the site to its knees on more than one occasion. The plugin handles catalogue syncing, feed generation, Meta tracking and related background processes, but provides no useful control over batching, throttling or scheduling resource-intensive sync jobs. In our case, catalogue/feed activity coincided with extremely aggressive meta-externalads crawling of the store, including hundreds of requests per minute. Combined with the plugin’s own sync/background workload, this generated enough load to destabilise Redis/object caching and make both the storefront and WordPress admin extremely slow or unavailable. Disabling the plugin immediately restored normal performance. There are also numerous reports from other users involving failed feed-generation jobs, repeated scheduled-action retries, excessive CPU usage and heavy catalogue syncing. For a small catalogue it may be fine, but I would be very cautious about running it on a larger WooCommerce store. We ultimately replaced it with separate dedicated plugins for Meta Pixel/CAPI tracking and catalogue feed generation, giving us much better control over each process.

review_examples.title: Silent failure during setup caused by blocked third-party cookies (1 star)
review_examples.description: Replies: 0 Rating: 1 star After struggling with this setup for far too long, and after the usual experience of trying to get help from the Meta Help Center (which was, unsurprisingly, not very helpful), I finally found the actual issue. The connection process fails if your browser blocks third-party cookies. The setup appears to work, shows that WooCommerce is connected to Facebook, and then the popup just goes black or gets stuck. There are no useful error messages, no clear indication of what went wrong, and the plugin logs only show that the access token is missing afterwards. The solution was to temporarily allow third-party cookies in the browser, complete the Meta connection, and then disable them again. A simple warning in the setup screen would have saved hours of troubleshooting. Expecting users to diagnose a silent OAuth failure caused by browser privacy settings is not exactly a great user experience.

support_examples.title: Meta Pixel not initializing with Meta for WooCommerce
support_examples.description: Replies: 1 Hello, I am having a problem with the Meta for WooCommerce plugin. The WooCommerce catalog is connected and products are syncing correctly, but the Meta Pixel is not initializing on my website and no events are received in Meta Events Manager. I have already contacted Meta Support, and they told me that the issue appears to be related to the WooCommerce plugin and that I should contact WooCommerce support. Here are the checks I have already performed: Meta for WooCommerce is connected correctly. The product catalog is syncing. Meta Pixel Helper does not detect any Pixel on the website. Meta Events Manager does not receive test events. fbevents.js loads correctly with HTTP status 200. typeof fbq returns function. fbq.getState() shows pixels: Array(0) and pixelInitializationTime: -1. The browser console shows a Meta Pixel warning saying that it is trying to set an argument for an uninitialized Pixel ID. I tested with the parent Hello Elementor theme instead of the child theme, but the problem remained. I tested Elementor Safe Mode, but the problem remained. JavaScript delay/defer options in LiteSpeed Cache are disabled. I also tested after accepting all cookies. It appears that the Meta Pixel library is loading, but the Pixel itself is never initialized. Could you please help me understand why Meta for WooCommerce is not initializing the Pixel and how to fix it? Thank you.

support_examples.title: Incorrect brand mapping for variable product variations
support_examples.description: Replies: 7 Hello, I’m experiencing an issue with the Brand field synchronization between WooCommerce and the Meta/Facebook Catalog when using the Meta for WooCommerce plugin. The brand is mapped correctly for the parent variable product . However, the individual variations of that product do not inherit the product’s brand . Instead, in the Meta Catalog I see: Parent variable product → Brand: correct product brand Individual variations → Brand: website/store name For example, if the WooCommerce product belongs to the brand Royal Canin , the parent product is correctly sent to Meta with Royal Canin as the brand, while its variations are sent with my website/store name as the brand. This affects all of my variable products and results in incorrect brand information in the Meta Catalog. Could you please help me determine why the variations are not inheriting the brand from their parent WooCommerce product? Ideally, I would like all variations to use the same Brand value as their parent product , rather than falling back to the website/store name. Is there a setting, mapping option, filter, or other recommended solution in Meta for WooCommerce that can correct this behavior? Thank you very much for your help.

support_examples.title: E-Invoicing Roadmap: Peppol, Spain, France and Other Countries
support_examples.description: Replies: 2 We’d like to share a brief overview of our current e-invoicing roadmap and the areas we’re actively working on. Peppol Our free PDF Invoices & Packing Slips for WooCommerce plugin already includes support for the Peppol BIS format. For businesses that also need to send documents through the Peppol Network, we offer a paid extension that provides the network connection and automation. This solution can be used in different countries where Peppol is part of the e-invoicing infrastructure, including Belgium and the Netherlands , among others. Spain For Spain, we are working together with Dixitalmedia on a VeriFactu compatibility extension . We are supporting their development work from the technical side to ensure compatibility with our plugin and its invoice data. France We are aware of the upcoming French e-invoicing requirements, and improving our support for France is one of our roadmap priorities. Currently, users can already generate invoices in Factur-X format with our free plugin when using the mPDF extension . Over the coming months, we plan to make significant improvements to our French e-invoicing implementation, including better compatibility with the applicable requirements and automation for sending documents through the relevant network infrastructure. Other countries E-invoicing requirements vary considerably between countries, and we are continuously evaluating where additional integrations and country-specific support are needed. If you have questions about support for a particular country or an upcoming e-invoicing requirement, please reach out to us directly. We’ll be happy to provide more information about the current possibilities and our plans. This topic was modified 2 days, 10 hours ago by alexmigf .

support_examples.title: 5.16.1 — order edit screen exhausts 256M PHP memory on some orders
support_examples.description: Replies: 2 Hello, Since some time (at least July 2026) the order edit screen returns a blank HTTP 500 on a subset of orders. Enabling WP_DEBUG_LOG gave a consistent fatal, identical on every attempt: PHP Fatal error: Allowed memory size of 268435456 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 1060864 bytes) in /wp-includes/functions.php on line 5581 Line 5581 is ob_end_flush() inside wp_ob_end_flush_all(), so the page finishes rendering and dies while flushing the output buffer. Isolated by bisection: with WooPayments, WooCommerce Shipping & Tax and Mondial Relay – InPost all active, the page loads. Adding PDF Invoices & Packing Slips reproduces the 500 every time. Raising WP_MAX_MEMORY_LIMIT to 768M makes the page load, so the consumption is large but bounded — not an infinite loop. Environment: WordPress 7.1 / WooCommerce 11.0.1 (legacy post storage, HPOS not enabled) PDF Invoices & Packing Slips 5.16.1 PHP 8.3.33, cgi-fcgi, OPcache disabled, memory_limit 256M Divi 4.27.8, 18 other plugins ~618 orders Two further observations that may help: Order data is clean. I checked 597 orders in a DB dump: 51,922 postmeta rows, 27,602 order itemmeta rows and 3,626 order notes, zero serialization or encoding anomalies, meta size per order very uniform (median 2.2 KB, max 3.8 KB). So this is not corrupted data. The plugin leaves stale options behind: 236 rows named wpo_ips_semaphore_lock_attach_doc_to_email_*_from_order_NNNN, all withvalue 0, two per order, never cleaned up. Happy to provide a Query Monitor profile if useful. Best regards,

review_examples.title: Pro features you already built stop working when the license expires (1 star)
review_examples.description: Replies: 1 Rating: 1 star I used Formidable Forms Pro for a client-facing site and built working forms with Pro fields, including sections. When my license expired, those existing forms became partially uneditable. Not “no new features” – I lost the ability to edit what I had already built and paid for. To be fair: front-end forms keep submitting, and the knowledge base does state you lose access to Pro features while expired. So this is technically documented. The problem is where it’s documented. The pricing page – the page you actually read before buying – says renewal is required for continued access to support, plugin updates, and new add-ons. Nothing about losing the ability to edit forms you already made. Two different messages in two places, and the softer one sits where the purchase decision happens. I understand paying for updates and support. That’s normal and fair. Locking editing access to work already completed under a valid license is a different thing, and it should be stated plainly on the pricing page rather than buried in a FAQ. Practical consequences for me: I won’t be renewing, I’ve stopped recommending the plugin to clients, and I’m migrating existing sites to an alternative. The plugin itself is capable and well built – that’s what makes this policy frustrating rather than merely disappointing. If you’re evaluating Formidable, budget for permanent yearly renewal, not a one-time purchase. Whatever you build, you keep the ability to run it, not to change it. atlassian.name: Zephyr - Test Management and Automation for Jira
atlassian.summary: Manage, reuse, and automate tests across projects—all inside Jira. Align teams and catch defects quickly with AI-powered, no-code automation. Gain full visibility with seamless test execution, cross-project sharing, and built-in reporting.

review_examples.body: I have had an excellent experience using SmartBear Zephyr for test management. It is a powerful and reliable tool that significantly improves the overall testing workflow. One of the standout features is its seamless integration with Jira, which makes it very easy to link test cases with user stories, track execution, and maintain full visibility of the testing process. This integration enhances collaboration between QA and development teams and keeps everything well-organized in one place. The
Very intuitive and easy to use. The call to test feature, customizable fields, ability to quickly select all test cases based on filters are very helpful.

I tried Zephyr and found it easy to use and well integrated with Jira. However, I decided not to adopt it because the licensing cost is based on all Jira users rather than just the QA team members who need it. For a team with only 4–5 QA engineers, the pricing was not cost-effective. I also found the feature set too basic for our testing and automation needs. Overall, it may be suitable for teams with simple requirements, but it was not the right fit for our organization.
Overall good test management solution, but has its flaws like all other solutions on the market.

At one point, we had trouble with an automation rule that used smart values in checklist items, but the support team quickly pointed out what was wrong and helped us configure it correctly. After that, everything worked exactly as expected. Overall, it’s an easy-to-use and surprisingly powerful checklist app
